text.p: England soccer international Steve Stone said on Friday he would not play again until October after his season-long comeback from a knee injury suffered a setback.
The Nottingham Forest midfielder, who ruptured his knee against Leicester in September, said his return to action had fallen behind schedule.
"A small problem in the knee developed a couple of months ago which may eventually set my comeback back a bit," said Stone.

"Doctors found something wrong with the way it was coming along and so it was a bit of a setback. I had been looking towards the start of the season as a possible comeback. I will join in pre-season training but I can't see myself playing any pre-season matches."
Stone's injury so early in the season played a part in Forest's slide towards relegation from the English premier league, which now looks a certainty. ----

LONDON, April 25 (Reuter) -- Friday's English tabloid newspapers followed Manchester United's European Cup semifinal defeat by Borussia Dortmund with a wave of speculation over the future of Eric Cantona.
The Frenchman's contract expires at the end of next season and he has not yet been offered an extension.
This has been seen as a sign that the club is prepared to release talismanic forward, who is 31 next month.

Headlines such as "Cantona Can Go," and "Au Revoir" in Friday's Sun and Daily Mail newspapers topped stories claiming the City interests in the club's public company could limit manager Alex Ferguson's influence in contract matters.
But club chairman Martin Edwards said on Friday there was no justification for the speculation.

Cantona joined United from Leeds for a bargain one million pounds ($1.6 million) in 1992 and was a major factor in the club's run of success over the past five years. His form has dipped this season but United still look certain to retain the premier league title. ----

LONDON, April 25 (Reuter) -- English third division soccer club Exeter City are hoping two energy-infused crystals from spoon-bending psychic Uri Geller will help them escape the drop out of the Football League.
Geller, whose son Daniel is an Exeter fan, has ordered one crystal to be placed behind each goal when the Devon side take on Chester City on Saturday.

"There are no guarantees in life but I am right 99.9 times out of a hundred," said Geller. "The crystals receive and transmit energy. I will be thinking of Exeter on Saturday and the crystals will transmit that energy to the pitch.
"It is very important for Exeter to win and I want to help them do it."
Exeter are five points clear of bottom club Brighton and a win over Chester will ensure league football for another season.
